traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 133 Euphorbiaceae: herbs, shrubs or trees, some with milky sap; leaves alternate, rarely opposite, simple or compound, sometimes reduced, mostly with stipules; flowers unisexual, mostly both sexes on one plant; petals mostly absent; stamens from one to a thousand; ovary mostly of three cells; fruit a capsule or a drupe. Hutchinson's family also holds what APG sets apart as Phyllanthaceae and Picrodendraceae; only characters that hold for the narrower family are stated, and the perianth (sepals only in most, none in Euphorbia's cyathium) is left for a value the vocabulary has.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 307, 309, 310, family Euphorbiaceae: inflorescence cyme, usually; read as {"cyme": "usually"}.
